No supplied paper directly proposes “a mix of slot-based training and preference optimization” specifically to detect political leaning in social posts. However, paper [2] does closely match the requested ingredients: it uses an interpretable slot-filling template for polarization detection and then applies DPO refinement with automatically generated preference pairs, reporting strong results on social-media polarization benchmarks.

Related but not exactly the same: paper [1] improves political stance detection in informal discourse by adding user profile context derived from historical posts, but it does not describe slot-based training or DPO. Paper [3] targets more granular “target-stance extraction” for political opinions in Reddit posts, evaluating LLM prompting strategies rather than slot-filling plus preference optimization.

So, only [2] provides the specific slot-filling plus preference-optimization recipe (DPO) in the context of social-text political polarization/leaning detection, while [1] and [3] cover context/prompting approaches without that training recipe.
